gloss: feudal lord; domain lord; daimyō of a han

definitions.gloss: feudal lord; domain lord; daimyō of a han
definitions.explanation: The lord who governed a han (feudal domain) during the Edo period of Japan. Each han was a semi-autonomous territory granted by the shogun.

examples.japanese: {藩主|はんしゅ}が{城|しろ}に{戻|もど}った。
examples.english: The feudal lord returned to the castle.

examples.japanese: この{藩|はん}の{藩主|はんしゅ}は{学問|がくもん}を{奨励|しょうれい}した。
examples.english: The lord of this domain promoted scholarship.

examples.japanese: {幕末|ばくまつ}には{多|おお}くの{藩主|はんしゅ}が{藩政改革|はんせいかいかく}に{取|と}り{組|く}んだ。
examples.english: At the end of the Edo period, many feudal lords undertook reforms of their domain's governance.

notes:
A term from the Edo period (1603–1868) referring to the ruler of a {藩|はん} (feudal domain). The {藩主|はんしゅ} held authority over governance, taxation, and military forces within the domain, but owed loyalty to the {将軍|しょうぐん} (shogun) in Edo.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {藩主|はんしゅ}の{命令|めいれい} — the lord's order
- {初代|しょだい}{藩主|はんしゅ} — the first lord (founder of the domain)
- {最後|さいご}の{藩主|はんしゅ} — the last lord (before abolition of domains)
- {藩主|はんしゅ}が{代|か}わる — the lord changes (succession)

RELATED TERMS:
- {大名|だいみょう} — feudal lord (broader term used across all periods of Japanese feudalism)
- {城主|じょうしゅ} — castle lord
